about: What app and plugin-package code may not do through "php/wordpress" (TypedPress\Wp\Guard at runtime, src/wordpress/mod.rs at build time). A name is compared after WordPress's own trim, lowercased (option_name is a case-insensitive column); a name with a byte outside printable ASCII is refused outright, because MySQL's unicode collations fold some of those onto ASCII names. `read: false` hides the option from get_option too.

options.name: active_plugins
options.why: WordPress loads every plugin it lists on the next request, so writing it runs PHP already on disk and passes sealed mode's activation check (wp-settings.php wp_get_active_and_valid_plugins)

options.name: active_sitewide_plugins
options.why: the network-active plugin list, loaded on every site of a network (wp_get_active_network_plugins)

options.name: recently_activated
options.why: wp-admin's record of plugin activations, which the plugins screen trusts

options.name: uninstall_plugins
options.why: maps plugins to the uninstall callbacks WordPress calls by name (uninstall_plugin)

options.name: auto_update_plugins
options.why: which plugins WordPress updates on its own

options.name: auto_update_themes
options.why: which themes WordPress updates on its own

options.name: template
options.why: the active theme's directory, whose functions.php WordPress loads (get_template_directory)

options.name: stylesheet
options.why: the active child theme's directory, whose functions.php WordPress loads (get_stylesheet_directory)

options.name: template_root
options.why: the theme root the active theme loads from (get_raw_theme_root)

options.name: stylesheet_root
options.why: the theme root the active child theme loads from (get_raw_theme_root)

options.name: current_theme
options.why: the active theme's name, kept with template and stylesheet

options.name: allowedthemes
options.why: the themes a network site may switch to

options.name: wplang
options.why: the locale, which picks the translation files WordPress includes as PHP (load_textdomain .l10n.php)

options.name: siteurl
options.why: where WordPress serves wp-admin and sign-in, so writing it moves sign-in to another host

options.name: home
options.why: the site's address, used for every link and redirect

options.name: admin_email
options.why: the address WordPress sends administrator mail and recovery-mode links to

options.name: new_admin_email
options.why: the pending administrator address a confirmation link activates

options.name: users_can_register
options.why: opens registration to anyone; with default_role it decides what every signup becomes

options.name: default_role
options.why: the role every new user gets, so `administrator` makes each signup an administrator

options.name: user_roles
options.why: `{prefix}user_roles` holds every role and its capabilities (WP_Roles)

options.name: site_admins
options.why: a network's super administrators

options.name: cron
options.why: WP-Cron's schedule: each entry calls a hook with stored arguments

options.name: upload_path
options.why: where uploads are written on disk (wp_upload_dir)

options.name: upload_url_path
options.why: the URL uploads are served from (wp_upload_dir)

options.name: db_version
options.why: WordPress runs its database upgrade when it differs

options.name: initial_db_version
options.why: WordPress's install version, which upgrades branch on

options.name: new_user_
options.why: a multisite invitation: maybe_add_existing_user_to_blog adds the stored user with the stored role when /newbloguser/<key>/ is visited

options.name: adminhash
options.why: the pending administrator-address change that a link with its hash confirms (wp-admin/options.php)

options.name: rewrite_rules
options.why: WordPress's compiled rewrite rules, which map every URL to a query

options.name: permalink_structure
options.why: the permalink structure every rewrite rule and link is built from

options.name: show_on_front
options.why: what the front page serves; TypedPress's pages own it

options.name: page_on_front
options.why: the front page TypedPress's pages manage

options.name: page_for_posts
options.why: the posts page TypedPress's pages manage

options.name: blog_public
options.why: whether search engines may index the site; the host sets it

options.name: fresh_site
options.why: WordPress's first-run flag, which decides starter content

options.name: comment_registration
options.why: whether commenting needs an account; with users_can_register it is part of sign-up policy

options.name: recovery_keys
options.why: recovery-mode keys, each one a way into a site with a fatal error

options.name: secret_key
options.why: the fallback key WordPress signs cookies and nonces with (wp_salt)

options.name: auth_key
options.why: a cookie-signing key WordPress stores as an option when wp-config.php has none (wp_salt)

options.name: auth_salt
options.why: a cookie-signing salt WordPress stores as an option when wp-config.php has none (wp_salt)

options.name: secure_auth_key
options.why: a cookie-signing key (wp_salt)

options.name: secure_auth_salt
options.why: a cookie-signing salt (wp_salt)

options.name: logged_in_key
options.why: a cookie-signing key (wp_salt)

options.name: logged_in_salt
options.why: a cookie-signing salt (wp_salt)

options.name: nonce_key
options.why: the nonce-signing key (wp_salt)

options.name: nonce_salt
options.why: the nonce-signing salt (wp_salt)

options.name: mailserver_pass
options.why: the post-by-email mailbox password

options.name: tp_
options.why: TypedPress's own options: schema state, the private-file signing secret (tp_runtime_secret), identity signing keys and webhook secrets

options.name: jetpack_
options.why: Jetpack's connection and module state; jetpack_active_modules loads module code, jetpack_options names the connection owner

options.name: _transient_
options.why: transients other code trusts as its own cache

options.name: _site_transient_
options.why: site transients, including update_plugins and update_themes, whose package URLs automatic updates download and install

options.name: secret
options.why: names a secret (jetpack_secrets, OAuth client secrets)

options.name: token
options.why: names a token (Jetpack's blog and user tokens in jetpack_private_options, API tokens)

options.name: private
options.why: names private data (jetpack_private_options, private keys)

options.name: password
options.why: names a password

options.name: passwd
options.why: names a password

options.name: credential
options.why: names credentials

options.name: api_key
options.why: names an API key

options.name: apikey
options.why: names an API key

options.name: access_key
options.why: names an access key

options.name: _salt
options.why: names a signing salt

postTypes.fieldsWhy: the catalog's postarr fields only: ID or import_id would overwrite an existing post (a TypedPress kind's included) and meta_input, tax_input and the rest write what no capability check covers
postTypes.why: wp_insert_post runs no capability check: a published customize_changeset applies its settings with the check turned off, and TypedPress's own tp_* types would skip the kinds' access rules. App code inserts posts and pages and other plugins' public types; TypedPress's kinds go through db
